question.text: Under Regulation 91(D)(1) and 91(D)(2) of LODR, a Social Enterprise listed on SSE is required to:

answer.text: Adopt SEBI's default list of 25 material events without modification.
File an event only after receiving written clearance from SEBI.
Delegate materiality determination entirely to the SSE's listing committee.
Frame its own policy for determination of materiality, duly approved by its board/management, and authorize one or more KMP to determine materiality.

explanation.text: **The Logic:** Reg 91(D)(1) requires the SE to frame a materiality policy approved by board/management and disclose it on SSE. 91(D)(2) requires authorisation of one or more KMPs to determine materiality and make disclosures; their contact details are also disclosed to SSE. **The Trap:** Main-board LODR Reg 30 has a 'deemed material' list - students borrow that concept here. SSE Reg 91(D) instead requires the SE to craft its own policy and name its own materiality-determining KMP. **Cross-Exam Context:** III-A/III-C tests Reg 30 materiality architecture (Para A + Para B + materiality policy). XXIII tests the SSE-specific 91(D) architecture - policy + KMP authorisation + 7-day disclosure. **Assessor's Pro-Tip:** During the AIR engagement, obtain a copy of the SE's board-approved materiality policy and a list of authorised KMPs. Any event the SIA identifies during fieldwork that was not disclosed within 7 days but is covered by the policy is a reportable deviation.
